<noinclude><pagequality level="4" user="Yann" />{{rh|168|AITAREYÂ-ARA''N''YAKA.|}}{{rule}}</noinclude><section begin="aranyaka1 adhyaya2" />VIII, 89, 1) (the word {{lang|sa-Latl|b''ri''hat}} occurs). Verily, {{lang|sa-Latl|b''ri''hat}} is {{lang|sa-Latl|mahat}} (great), and as endowed with {{lang|sa-Latl|mahat}}, the form of this day is perfect.

13. In (the Pragâtha) {{lang|sa-Latl|naki''h'' sudâso ratham pary âsa na rîramad}} (Rv. VII, 32, 10) the words {{lang|sa-Latl|paryâsa }} (he moved round) and {{lang|sa-Latl|na rîramad}} (he did not enjoy) occur, and as endowed with the words {{lang|sa-Latl|paryasta}} and {{lang|sa-Latl|rânti}} the form of this day is perfect<ref>Because the performance of the Mahâvrata sacrifices moves the worshipper round to another world and gives him enjoyment. Comm. It is difficult to surpass the absurdity of these explanations. {{lang|sa-Latl|Na rîramat}} means no one stopped the chariot of Sudâs. But even if it meant that no one rejoiced through the chariot of the Sudâs, it would be difficult to see how the negative of enjoyment, mentioned in the hymn, could contribute to the perfection of a sacrifice which is to confer positive enjoyment on the worshipper.</ref>.

He recites all (these) Pragâthas, in order to obtain all the days (of the sacrifice), all the Ukthas<ref>The stotras following after the Ya''g''ñâya''g''ñîya Sâman, serving for the ukthya-kratus.</ref>, all the P''ri''sh''th''as<ref>The strotras of the noon-libation, to be performed with the Rathantara, B''ri''hat, and other Sâmans.</ref>, all the ''S''astras<ref>The ''s''astras, recitations, accompanying the oblations of â''g''ya.</ref>, all the Pra-ugas<ref>The pra-ugas, a division of ''s''astras, described above.</ref>, and all the Savanas (libations).


{{sh|{{sc|{{Anchor+|Khanda2|Second Kha''nd''a}}<ref>The type after which the Marutvatîya-''s''astra is to be performed is the ''K''aturvi''m''sa day. Hitherto (from {{lang|sa-Latl|â tvâ ratham}} to {{lang|sa-Latl|naki''h'' sudâsa''h''}}), all that is taken over from the type to the modification, i. e. the Marutvatîya, has been explained. Now follow the verses which are new and perculiar to the Marutvatîya of the Mahâvrata.</ref>.}}}}

1. He recites the hymn, {{lang|sa-Latl|asat su me ''g''arita''h'' sâbhivega''h''}} (Rv. X, 27, 1), (and in it the word) {{lang|sa-Latl|satya-dhv''ri''tam}}, the destroyer of truth. Verily, that day
